386 DX 40 MHz
Recreation of My First PC. Had a case just like this one and contents as close as I could match for reasonable money. Beefed up with 4 extra MB of RAM, CF Card for harddisk and a modern Optical drive. The SB Pro 2 CT1600 is my own original from my original 386 DX 40 in 1993 (the sound card was added in 1994). The case front and the Diamond Stealth 24 ET4000 VLB are equal to my original.

486 DX2 66MHz
Bought in Engesvang in 1998 for nostalgia. Original harddisk still inside, but disconnected, in favour of a 4GB early SSD. The BIOS could not read it, so using XTIDE on the network card, to make the computer recognize the disk. Repairs on the motherboard (see photos) was done before I bought it. Bought to have a DOS compatible machine back when Windows 9x was on the rise.

Pentium III 500MHz
Uber scene and game machine with GUS, AWE32 with OPL3 chip, Voodoo2 and TNT2. All in a modern case with a window in the side to behold the hardware in action. An alternative Pentium II 333MHz can replace the PIII in the same setup. The machine is meant for demo scene and late DOS and early Windows game compatibility.

Pentium 4 3GHz (LGA775)
Very high end Win98 and also good for Windows XP. For max compatibility, both Windows 98 and XP have emulated Voodoo drivers using dgVoodoo and nGlide. My first retro gaming machine attempt, which also runs DOS with SB compatible drivers. However the machines with real ISA sound cards took it's place for DOS gaming. The CPU is a SL9KG Cedar Mill P4 that runs pretty cool compared to Prescott CPUs

AMD Athlon 5350 2GHz
SFF mikrotower XP machine with 64Bit OS specs, but with Windows XP 32 bit installed, to run the most demanding XP games. The SFF case has only a single slot space for a GPU, so chose the Quadro K2000, which has official XP drivers and is one of the latest and fastest GPU's for XP. Only surpassed by the K2200, which does not have official XP drivers, and the GTX 750 which is very rare as a single slot card.
